passage:
In the girls' hostel of the boarding school in Shillong, Maria found out at dinner that Nandini had told the whole dorm about her crush. Back in her room, face burning, she typed fast into the class group: 'Nandini can't keep one secret. Don't tell her anything.' Three friends reacted with laughing faces within seconds. For a moment it felt great.
By lights-out, Nandini was crying in the bathroom, and Maria's stomach had turned to stone. She deleted the message, but twenty-eight people had already seen it.
Next morning the counsellor, Ms Kharkongor, listened to both girls. Afterwards she said to Maria, 'Angry messages feel urgent. Try this rule: type it, don't send it, sleep on it.'
Maria wrote it on a sticky note and stuck it to her phone cover.

qa.q: How many people had already seen Maria's message before it was deleted?
qa.a: Twenty-eight people had already seen it.

qa.q: What did Maria feel by lights-out, and what caused the change?
qa.a: Maria felt heavy regret, her stomach like stone, after hearing Nandini crying in the bathroom.

qa.q: What choice did Maria make after the counsellor's advice?
qa.a: She wrote the rule 'type it, don't send it, sleep on it' on a sticky note and stuck it to her phone cover.

qa.q: How might Nandini have felt seeing the message in the class group?
qa.a: Nandini likely felt humiliated and hurt at being called out in front of the class, even if sharing the secret was wrong.

grounding: Shows a teenager sending an angry message in the heat of the moment, regretting it, and adopting a sleep-on-it rule.

subtype: Spending, posting or fighting in the moment [Actor]
passage:
Dear Anand bhaiya,
Remember the birthday money Nani gave me, the money I was saving for the art course? It's gone. On Saturday at the mall, my friends kept saying how cool the glowing headphones were, a sale was ending in ten minutes, my heart was pounding, and I just paid. All of it.
For one evening I felt amazing. By Sunday I felt sick. They're just headphones. The art course starts next month.
You always say you wait a night before any big buy. I used to think that was boring. Now I get it: when I'm excited and everyone's watching, my brain doesn't look past the next ten minutes.
So I'm making it my rule too. Anything that costs more than I spend in a week, I sleep on first.
I'm going to tell Nani myself this weekend.
Damini

qa.q: What was the birthday money from Nani meant for?
Why did Damini pay for the headphones so quickly?
qa.a: Excitement, friends calling the headphones cool and a sale ending in ten minutes made Damini's heart pound, so Damini acted without looking past the moment.

qa.q: What rule does Damini choose now, and why might it help?
qa.a: Sleeping on anything that costs more than a week's spending gives the excitement time to cool, so Damini can see past the next ten minutes.

qa.q: How might Anand bhaiya feel reading that the 'boring' habit now makes sense to Damini?
qa.a: Anand bhaiya might feel pleased and a little amused, and glad Damini is owning the mistake and planning to tell Nani.

grounding: Shows a teenager making a rash purchase under excitement and peer pressure, regretting it, and adopting a sleep-on-it rule.
